evidence: Mechanism fully documented AND implemented in /home/gio/tese/simulation/live51/planner_live_patch.py (docstring lines 1-24): the live planner's FpmEventSubscriber runs in tracking mode and keeps only the LAST forward-pass metric per worker per load tick (get_recent_stats), whereas offline replay feeds EVERY non-idle pass (replay_adapter _feed_extra_fpm_to_regression). Only mixed prefill+decode passes inform the aggregated (Mixed) capacity regression; at calm load these are rare events, so the last-per-tick sample almost never captures one and the Mixed store starves -> throughput scaling reports model_not_ready indefinitely. The code records the measured extreme: 'zero mixed samples in 5 minutes at 2 req/s' while the offline twin is ready at first tick; consistent with the tex's ~1%-of-calm-samples framing. This is a genuine causal mechanism (sampling policy drops the exact samples the capacity model needs), verifiable in code, and correctly attributed as a harness gap not a policy choice.
